features.name: any_comment_challenges_assumption
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly challenge an underlying assumption or premise of the OP's view, not merely dispute its factual conclusion?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Read title and argument to identify the OP's stated view and its underlying assumptions/premises. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertion (not a quotation merely of others unless adopted), explicitly questions or rejects an underlying assumption, premise, definition or value framing that the OP's reasoning relies on. Return 0 if comments exist but none do (including comments that only dispute facts or the conclusion). Return 0 for an empty list; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements and any post-outcome reports as evidence.

features.name: any_comment_challenges_conclusion_only
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment dispute the OP's factual claims or conclusion without challenging an underlying assumption?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. Read title and argument for the OP's view. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertion, disputes the OP's factual claims or conclusion without explicitly challenging an underlying assumption or premise within that comment. Else 0. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed gives null. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements and post-outcome reports as evidence.

h0: any_comment_challenges_assumption has no association with view-change rate, controlling for any_comment_challenges_conclusion_only.
h1: Discussions with any_comment_challenges_assumption = 1 have a higher view-change rate, controlling for any_comment_challenges_conclusion_only.
note: Operational assumptions: "challenge assumptions rather than just factual conclusions" is measured as presence of an assumption-challenging comment, with a conclusion-only presence control; the two are not mutually exclusive and the coefficient is not a strict contrast. Comment order/timing unknown; text may contain outcome announcements (excluded in the semantic specs). Associations only; the OLS on a binary outcome is a linear probability model.
